summary: Meta reiterated full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance of roughly 115 billion dollars, with the bulk earmarked for AI data centres and supporting infrastructure. The guide extends the multi-gigawatt campus buildout pattern set by Hyperion and Prometheus.

OpenAI expanded its multi-year compute capacity agreement with CoreWeave, adding roughly 12 billion dollars of contracted GPU capacity through 2030. The deal deepens the neocloud layer's role as overflow capacity for frontier labs.

The Space Development Agency awarded Rocket Lab a contract worth approximately 515 million dollars to design and build satellites for a proliferated low-earth-orbit defence constellation tranche. The award continues the pattern of national-security work flowing to newer launch-and-satellite primes.

GE Vernova committed roughly 600 million dollars to expand US manufacturing of transformers, switchgear, and grid equipment, citing multi-year order backlogs driven by data-centre interconnection queues. Lead times for large power transformers remain measured in years.

TSMC reaffirmed its expanded US investment program of approximately 165 billion dollars covering additional Arizona fabs, advanced packaging facilities, and an R&D centre. The program concentrates leading-edge capacity additions where AI accelerator demand is strongest.

The Department of Defense advanced its microreactor pilot program with Oklo for a powerhouse installation at a remote air base, continuing the federal pattern of acting as first customer for advanced fission. Licensing and fuel availability remain the gating items.

NASA awarded Redwire a contract of approximately 45 million dollars for in-space manufacturing and servicing technology demonstrations. The award adds to a string of small agency contracts that keep early in-space services companies funded ahead of commercial demand.

The Department of Energy awarded Energy Fuels roughly 80 million dollars to expand rare earth separation capacity at its White Mesa mill, part of the federal push to build non-Chinese midstream processing. Domestic separation capacity remains the chain's tightest link.

Vertiv agreed to acquire a privately held liquid-cooling and coolant-distribution specialist for roughly 600 million dollars, deepening its direct-to-chip thermal portfolio. Consolidation in cooling continues as rack densities climb past air-cooling limits.

Microsoft and Constellation Energy progressed their 20-year power purchase agreement covering 835 MW of nuclear output tied to the Crane Clean Energy Center restart, with deliveries ramping toward 2028. Hyperscaler PPAs for firm clean power remain the template other utilities are chasing.

The Department of Defense expanded its offtake and price-floor arrangement with MP Materials covering rare earth magnet output, committing roughly 400 million dollars across the agreement. The deal extends the public-private template for de-risking domestic magnet supply.

The Department of Energy extended its HALEU enrichment contract with Centrus Energy by roughly 110 million dollars, keeping the Piketon cascade producing fuel for advanced reactor demonstrations. Centrus remains the only licensed US HALEU producer.

The US Army placed a production order of approximately 25 million dollars with Red Cat Holdings under its short-range reconnaissance drone program. Small-drone procurement continues to shift toward US-made platforms from emerging vendors.

Amazon guided 2026 capital expenditure to roughly 125 billion dollars, dominated by AWS data-centre, custom-silicon, and power infrastructure spend. Management framed AI capacity as supply-constrained rather than demand-constrained.

US carriers expanded strategic investments and prepayments in AST SpaceMobile by roughly 350 million dollars to accelerate the direct-to-device satellite constellation buildout. Carrier capital continues to substitute for dilutive equity raises in the space segment.
